findings.title: New module lacks future annotations import
findings.problem: code-quality.md (Types And Imports) requires new modules to add 'from __future__ import annotations'. The new module src/codemie_tools/base/image_constants.py, added by this change, has no such import.
findings.impact: This breaks a documented project standard for new modules. No gate catches it: the Ruff select list in pyproject.toml has no FA rule. The code-quality standards row is therefore partial.
findings.recommendation: Add `from __future__ import annotations` directly below the module docstring and before the constants, as code-quality.md (Types And Imports) requires for new modules.

findings.title: Image-download concern appended to tools.py
findings.problem: code-quality.md (Module Cohesion) says a new concern with its own constants and pure functions goes into a new module next to its user. This change appends the whole GitLab image-download concern to the existing tools.py, which grows from 199 to 328 lines: IMAGE_STREAM_CHUNK_BYTES, UNINFORMATIVE_CONTENT_TYPES, _UPLOAD_MIME_TYPES (lines 39-44), GitlabMultimodalResponse (90-101) and _image_mime_for/_detect_image_mime/_read_image_bounded/_image_response (261-313).
findings.impact: This breaks a documented, blocking project standard. The guide records the same pattern being extracted later at extra cost.
findings.recommendation: Move IMAGE_STREAM_CHUNK_BYTES, UNINFORMATIVE_CONTENT_TYPES, _UPLOAD_MIME_TYPES, GitlabMultimodalResponse and the detect/read/wrap helpers (_detect_image_mime, _read_image_bounded, the artifact building in _image_response) into a sibling module such as src/codemie_tools/core/vcs/gitlab/image_download.py, and import them from tools.py.

findings.title: Extension fallback branches not pinned by tests
findings.problem: Regression gap: two documented branches of _detect_image_mime have no test. The text/plain member of UNINFORMATIVE_CONTENT_TYPES is never exercised, because the fallback tests send only application/octet-stream or no Content-Type. The '/uploads/' restriction at lines 279-280 is also unpinned: every octet-stream or missing-Content-Type case uses UPLOAD_PATH, and the non-upload GETs carry no image extension. So deleting 'text/plain' from the set, or removing or widening the '/uploads/' guard, leaves every test green.
findings.impact: Consumer: GitlabTool.execute GETs on upload and non-upload paths. If the text/plain branch regresses, uploads served as text/plain come back as a latin-1 text dump instead of an artifact. If the /uploads/ guard regresses, non-upload binary endpoints served as octet-stream (e.g. job artifact files with a .png name) become image artifacts. In both cases no test fails.
findings.recommendation: In test_image_download.py, add (a) a `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` response on an `/uploads/.../x.png` path and assert a GitlabMultimodalResponse with mime_type image/png, and (b) an `application/octet-stream` response on a non-upload path ending in `.png` (e.g. `/api/v4/projects/1/jobs/2/artifacts/out/screenshot.png`) and assert the plain HttpResult string comes back.

findings.title: Streamed response not closed on read error
findings.problem: Every GET now opens with stream=True. _image_response calls response.close() only on the oversize path. If iter_content in _read_image_bounded raises mid-stream (ChunkedEncodingError, ConnectionError, ReadTimeout), the response is never closed. execute catches only TypeError/JSONDecodeError, so the raw network error escapes. No test asserts close(): the oversize tests use bare Mocks, so deleting the existing response.close() also leaves every test green.
findings.impact: Each image GET that fails mid-stream leaves a half-read pooled connection checked out until garbage collection. This is a resource-lifecycle defect on a live path for every GitLab image download. The missing close() assertion means the oversize release can regress silently.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the bounded read in `_image_response` in try/finally (or `with response:`) so the response is closed whenever the body is not fully consumed, including when iter_content raises ChunkedEncodingError, ConnectionError or a read timeout. In both oversize tests add `response.close.assert_called_once()`, and add a test where iter_content raises mid-stream that asserts close() is still called.

findings.title: Image body not validated before attaching
findings.problem: _image_response base64-encodes whatever body it read and labels it with the detected MIME type. It never checks that the body is non-empty or that it starts with the image format's signature. A 2xx image response with a 0-byte body produces an artifact with empty data. An upload served as octet-stream, text/plain or with no Content-Type is attached as an image based on its file extension alone, even when the body is not that image. image_artifact_hook._extract_image_blocks forwards data/mime_type into an ImageContentBlock with no validation.
findings.impact: An empty or non-image payload reaches the multimodal model as an image, and the provider may reject the whole model call, not just the image. Reachability is unconfirmed: it depends on GitLab or an object-storage redirect serving an empty or mislabelled upload body.
findings.recommendation: Before building the artifact, return a text-only GitlabMultimodalResponse (status line plus "Empty image body; skipped." or "Body is not a valid <mime> image; skipped.", image_artifacts=[]) when the body is empty or its leading bytes do not match the expected format signature (PNG \x89PNG, JPEG \xff\xd8\xff, GIF GIF87a/GIF89a, WebP RIFF....WEBP). Cover the empty-body and mismatched-signature cases in test_image_download.py.

findings.title: user_description lacks example and origin note
findings.problem: The spec (Description) requires both GITLAB_TOOL.description and user_description to gain an IMAGE RESPONSES section, an example GET request for a project upload, and a note that absolute URLs must share the configured GitLab origin. The original task's AC8 asks for the same in both fields. description meets all three. user_description gains only a one-line IMAGE RESPONSES bullet (lines 106-107), with no example request and no same-origin note.
findings.impact: A required spec item ships partial. Users reading the tool's user-facing description get no upload example and are not told that absolute URLs on a foreign origin are rejected.
findings.recommendation: Extend the IMAGE RESPONSES section of GITLAB_TOOL.user_description with an example GET request for a project upload (e.g. `/<namespace>/<project>/uploads/<secret>/<file>.png` or `/api/v4/projects/:id/uploads/:secret/:filename`) and a note that absolute URLs must share the configured GitLab origin, as `description` already does. Keep every substring that test_tools_vars.py already asserts.
